changes.reason: '2.4.64' is the Apache httpd release version in which the 'optional' SSLEngine argument was removed, not a quantity with a missing unit space. Reformatting it would misrepresent the version number.
semanticInvariants: the version number 2.4.64 must remain byte-identical

changes.reason: 'RFC 2817' is a specific IETF document citation (like the FIPS 140-2 and CFR citations elsewhere in this corpus), not a general term being repeatedly used that benefits from first-use expansion. It appears exactly once, as part of a fixed document number, and is never referred to again.

'SSL/TLS' is the fixed, compound name of the protocol pairing this directive controls ('SSL/TLS Protocol Engine'), not an ambiguous and/or slash between two independent words. Rewriting it as 'SSL or TLS' or 'SSL and TLS' would change the established product/protocol name and could misleadingly suggest the engine handles only one of the two.
semanticInvariants: the compound protocol name 'SSL/TLS' must remain unchanged everywhere it appears

changes.reason: This ellipsis is inside a literal Apache configuration example ('<VirtualHost _default_:443> / SSLEngine on / #... / </VirtualHost>'), where '#...' is the conventional config-comment placeholder meaning 'other directives go here'. It is example syntax, not prose, and editing it would corrupt the example. The tool now agrees: the document reader (issue #25) parses the whole '<VirtualHost>...</VirtualHost>' construct as one opaque HTML block instead of masking only its opening and closing tag lines, so 'SSLEngine on' and '#...' are no longer read as prose at all and the finding no longer occurs, so expectedDiagnostics is empty. The prose was left unchanged.
semanticInvariants: the VirtualHost configuration example, including the '#...' placeholder comment, must remain byte-identical

changes.reason: The flagged occurrence is inside the SSLFIPS directive reference heading ('SSLFIPS / SSL FIPS mode Switch / Syntax: SSLFIPS on|off ...'), where 'FIPS' is part of the literal directive name and the C API symbol 'FIPS_mode' used later, and reappears afterward only inside the fixed citation 'FIPS 140-2'. There is no ordinary-prose occurrence where expanding it would not require altering a protected identifier (SSLFIPS, FIPS_mode) or a citation number (FIPS 140-2).
semanticInvariants: the directive name SSLFIPS, the C symbol FIPS_mode, and the citation 'FIPS 140-2' must all remain byte-identical

changes.reason: '140-2' is part of the fixed standard number 'FIPS 140-2', a NIST publication citation, not a quantity with a missing unit space. Inserting a space would corrupt the standard's name.
semanticInvariants: the standard citation 'FIPS 140-2' must remain byte-identical everywhere it appears

We split it into four short sentences at its existing clause boundaries ('for specific requirements' / semicolon / 'but may be described' / 'when all components') without reordering any clause or dropping any of the three 'FIPS 140-2' citations, so every requirement and every citation is preserved in its original order.

notes: Six of seven diagnostics are false positives against version numbers, standard/document citation numbers, a fixed compound protocol name, a literal configuration-example placeholder, and directive-name identifiers; only the one genuinely overlong, semicolon-joined descriptive sentence is rewritten, preserving every identifier and citation in it.

candidateAdjudications.quote:
SSLEngine
SSL Engine Operation Switch
Syntax: SSLEngine
candidateAdjudications.reason: The span joins the directive name SSLEngine to its title line 'SSL Engine Operation Switch' and the following 'Syntax: SSLEngine' declaration across line breaks; all three are component identity and reference-page boilerplate (a directive name, its title, and its syntax label), not a prose noun pile a reader must parse.
'Context: server config, virtual host' is a labelled metadata field listing two established httpd configuration scopes, comma-separated; there is no ambiguous grouping for a reader to guess.
'Support ... was removed in 2.4.64' is descriptive release history, not an instruction; the actor (the httpd developers) is irrelevant and naming them would add nothing.

The only sensible referent for 'It enabled RFC 2817 support' is the 'optional' argument (or, equivalently, support for it); reading 'It' as the version 2.4.64 contradicts the same sentence, so the competing readings do not change the meaning.
'SSL/TLS Protocol Engine' is the capitalised component name mod_ssl uses for itself; component identity outranks simplification.
The bare 'This' parallels 'This directive' in the immediately preceding sentence, and only a directive can be 'used inside a VirtualHost section'; the engine and the usage do not fit the predicate.
Second occurrence of the established component name 'SSL/TLS Protocol Engine'; a real product/component name is never a noun-cluster defect.

Re-reviewed after the leading 'SSLFIPS' and 'SSL FIPS' identifiers became protected regions, which shortened this candidate from 777-821 to 794-821. What is left is the tail of the directive's title line ('... mode Switch') stitched across a line break onto the following 'Syntax: SSLFIPS' declaration label. 'mode Switch' alone is two words and under the limit; the run only reaches four content words by crossing the newline into a reference-page metadata field. Two adjacent layout fields, not a noun pile a reader must parse — the same structural artefact as the SSLEngine heading above, on a narrower span.

'It must be set in the global server context' follows a sentence containing both 'This directive' and 'the SSL library FIPS_mode flag'; proximity favours the flag but the truth is the SSLFIPS directive, and the two readings tell the reader to configure different things.
The passive states a placement constraint on the directive (where it must appear), not an action assigned to an actor; who edits the configuration file is immaterial to the constraint.
'If httpd was compiled against an SSL library ...' is a descriptive condition about an existing build; whoever compiled httpd is genuinely unknown and naming an actor would be misleading.
'may be described as ...' is a careful compliance statement in descriptive prose where the describing party is deliberately unnamed; supplying an actor would change the claim.

'when all components are assembled and operated under the guidelines' is a compliance condition, not an instruction; the agent is intentionally generic because the condition holds regardless of who performs it.
